correctness.rationale: For \(k\ge5\) and \(|n|\le F_{k-4}\), direct lower bounds exclude all but the prefixes \((1,0,-1)\) and \((-1,0,1)\); their lower signed digits map bijectively to \(d_i\in\{0,1,2\}\), giving \(n=\pm(1+\sum d_iF_i)\). The \(n=0\) case vanishes; weights beyond index \(k-3\) are too large to affect the required coefficient. The summatory count is trapped between \(3^{J-4}\) and \(3^J\) whenever \(F_J\le X-1<F_{J+1}\), implying exponent \(\log 3/\log\varphi\) by Binet. The attached verifier compares forbidden-prefix counts, direct four-term differences, bounded-digit coefficients, and finite growth bounds using exact integers.

value.rationale: The motivating paper treats the eventually constant signed-Fibonacci correction as a mysterious integer sequence. An all-integer generating product gives its values and explicit finite computation, a uniform effective stabilization threshold replaces unspecified sufficiently large length, and the summatory exponent supplies a globally quantified behavior for the precise object. These are natural structural questions motivated by the published recurrence rather than arbitrary coefficient slices; no pointwise or asymptotic-constant claim is made.
